Single-investigator source checks

One investigator worked through both written lists. These checks let a reader reproduce the counts, retrace a possible route, and see where the source leaves a question open.

What changed between the lists?

The first snapshot has 16 entries. The expanded snapshot preserves those 16 and adds 20. The number 36 counts descriptions in the expanded list.

To count immediate exits from the puddle, follow only entries that start there. The first list has three, through soil, runoff, and evaporation. In the second list, entry 21 adds a drinking bird. That makes four immediate exits.

Can the same transfer appear at two scales?

Entry 12 says plant water reaches fruit. Entry 19 specifies water moving from the stem into developing fruit. Counting the descriptions gives two entries. Both can describe one transfer.

What does a return to the bird establish?

Follow droppings to soil, soil to roots, roots to stem, stem to fruit, and fruit to a bird. The route returns to a bird in the model. Identifying the same individual in a garden would require an observation.

Where does the source leave a gap?

Entry 18 ends inside a growing leaf. Entry 3 begins with a drop on its surface. The list supplies no transfer between those two locations. The investigator leaves that join open.
